messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

3. offer apple slices or a pear, depending on the delivery
4. keep the yogurt separate for students who don't want it on top

Helen: also, the delivery note says pears are expected wednesday, but the fruit company has changed the date twice this month. we can use apples from storage if the pears don't show up. those apples are the smaller kind, so the serving count may need a quick check.

Omar: facilities measured the cooler area this morning. there's room for a second tray cart, but we'd need to move the recycling bin about three feet. that might ease the line, though it won't help if students all wait for the hot entree at once.

Priya: on the survey comments, a few students asked whether the chickpea bowl could be dairy-free. the draft has yogurt as an optional topping, so that seems possible, but we should verify the sauce ingredients before describing it that way. the printed menu goes out monday.

Jess: i talked to the two lunch aides on the first shift. they can manage a separate topping cup, but they'd rather not add another ladle to the line. one suggested pre-filling small cups during setup; she'd need to know how many to prepare by 9:30.

Maya: got it. the count from the last taste test was 54 students, and 31 picked the bowl as their favorite. it was a small group, and the sample came with a roll, so i don't want to treat that as a forecast for a full lunch period.

Ben: for allergies, the chickpea bowl draft lists sesame in the dressing, and the current wrap has wheat and milk. the kitchen posts the allergen sheet by the register. if we change the dressing, we need the updated ingredient label before the sheet is printed.

Luis: the prep sheet says the bowl takes about 24 minutes of staff time for one batch, not counting the potatoes. the wrap takes less hands-on time, but tortillas have to be warmed in batches. i can ask the kitchen lead whether those estimates include cleanup.

Omar: one thing i noticed during the test: the students who took the bowl asked for more rice, but there wasn't a second scoop set out. we had enough rice in the kitchen. might be useful to put the serving amount on the test card next time, so we're comparing the same portions.

Helen: the budget sheet uses $2.18 per serving for the wrap and $1.96 for the bowl, based on the vendor prices we have now. that doesn't include the optional yogurt cup or any extra labor. purchasing said those prices are good through the end of the month.

Priya: should we ask the kitchen to run the chickpea bowl as a Tuesday test next week, if the potatoes can be prepped Monday and the allergen label is confirmed? the survey and taste test are useful, but neither tells us how it will move through the regular line.

Maya: that's the question i need to send to the committee, along with the oven and staffing caveats. please flag anything i've missed before 2 pm tomorrow. i can ask for a test only, not a permanent menu change, and i'll include the counts as context rather than a promise of demand.
